title: A/B testing: hypothesis, primary metric and success criterion

videos.script: Panela redesigned its checkout page. A month later, orders were up eleven per cent. Did the page do it? {{question}} Nobody can say. The month after the launch was also the month after Carnival, in a business that was growing, in a season that was getting busier. {{confounded}} Any of those could be the eleven per cent. In the same weeks of the year before, with no new page at all, orders rose ten. {{lastyear}} An A/B test answers the question by changing one thing for half the visitors, at random, at the same time. Everything else, the season, the trend, the holiday, falls on both halves alike. {{random}} But a test is only as good as the question it was built to answer. Before the first visitor sees anything, three things have to be written down. What you expect and why. The one number that decides. And the result that would make you ship it. {{three}} This lesson is those three things. The next four are how to run the test and read it. {{end}}
